before.title: 3.5L V6 Cold-Start Ticking / Valve-Train Rattle
before.description: Owners of 3.5L Lambda III V6 Carnivals report a distinct ticking or rattling noise for a few seconds on cold start that fades as the engine warms and oil pressure builds. Reported root causes include the timing-chain tensioner briefly losing its prime, the high-pressure GDI fuel pump, and VVT/cam gear chatter until oil pressure rises. Some owners had belts, tensioners, alternators and oil pumps replaced without resolution while others were told it is normal GDI-pump noise.
before.solution: Have a dealer document the noise and compare against known-good vehicles; if it is the timing-chain tensioner losing prime, warranty replacement of the tensioner/guides resolves it. Using the correct spec oil and confirming proper oil pressure helps VVT-related chatter. Persistent, loud metallic knocking (versus a brief tick) warrants deeper inspection to rule out timing-component wear before warranty expires.
symptoms: Ticking or rattle for a few seconds at cold start
Noise disappears once warm
Louder after sitting overnight
Valve-train / GDI pump tapping

before.title: A/C Compressor Premature Failure and Weak Cooling (Service Action SA632)
before.description: Owners report the air conditioning gradually losing cooling or quitting entirely, sometimes at low mileage. Kia issued service action SA632 for certain 2025-2026 Carnivals citing excessive clearance between the compressor piston and cylinder that reduces its ability to compress refrigerant. Separately, earlier (2022-2024) owners report DVE18C compressor failures with internal shorts, occasionally denied as not covered, with replacements quoted around $1,400. The compressor is the costliest A/C component, so weak-cooling complaints carry high repair exposure. The OEM compressor is part 97701-R0100 (DVE18C, 6-groove belt-driven).
before.solution: Confirm whether the VIN is covered by SA632 or any A/C campaign first (free repair). For non-campaign failures, have the system pressure-tested to confirm compressor failure vs. refrigerant leak or A/C control-valve/connector fault before replacing. Use OEM compressor 97701-R0100. Replace the receiver/drier and flush the system when the compressor is changed to avoid debris-induced repeat failures.
symptoms: Warm or weak air from vents
Intermittent cooling that comes and goes
A/C clutch not engaging
Unusual noise from compressor
Higher cabin humidity

before.description: Owners report the Carnival stalling or losing motive power while driving, sometimes in moving traffic, frequently accompanied by an illuminated check-engine light. Check-engine light illuminates

before.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Clog Causing Wet Headliner / Interior Water Leak
before.description: Carnivals with the panoramic sunroof can leak water into the cabin, showing up as a wet headliner or damp footwells after heavy rain. The sunroof relies on corner drain tubes that route water down the pillars; debris clogs the tubes (or seals age/misalign), so water backs up and overflows into the interior. Owners report wet headliners the dealer could not immediately diagnose. Left unchecked, trapped water causes mildew and can affect electronics.
before.solution: Clear the sunroof drain tubes with low-pressure compressed air or a soft flexible line to flush debris from the corner drains; confirm water exits at the bottom of the pillars. Replace aged or damaged sunroof seals and re-align the glass if gaps exist. Dry the headliner/carpet promptly to prevent mold and inspect for any water that reached body electrical connectors.

Water dripping from A-pillars or dome light
Damp carpet or footwells
Musty smell from trapped moisture

before.title: Premature Front Brake Rotor Warping and Pedal Pulsation
before.description: Multiple owners report front brake rotors warping early, producing steering-wheel/brake-pedal pulsation and vibration under braking, with some reporting recurrence even after rotors are replaced or resurfaced. Owners with repeat warping report better longevity using premium/upgraded rotors and pads and avoiding hard braking from high speed when fully loaded. Bed in new pads/rotors properly.

Vibration when slowing from highway speed
Squealing or grinding from front brakes
Uneven/premature pad wear
Longer stopping distances

before.title: Power Sliding Door Auto-Reverse Failure Causing Injuries
before.description: The power sliding rear doors on the Kia Carnival may fail to auto-reverse when contacting an obstruction such as a person, child, or pet. The pinch sensors along the door edge require excessive force to trigger, allowing the door to continue closing on an occupant before finally reversing. Kia recalled 51,568 units (2022-2023 models built between Jan 2021 and Feb 2023) under NHTSA campaign 23V-179, and at least 9 injuries were confirmed including one broken arm and a fractured thumb. A class-action lawsuit alleges the recall fix was insufficient.
before.solution: Visit a Kia dealer for the recall software update (NHTSA 23V-179) that adds warning chimes and slows the door closing speed near the fully closed position. If the issue persists after the update, request the dealer inspect and recalibrate the pinch sensor strips along the door edges. Document any continued incidents carefully for warranty or legal claims.
symptoms: Power sliding door does not reverse when contacting a person or object
Door closes with excessive force before finally reversing
No warning chime when door is closing on an obstruction
Door pinch sensor appears unresponsive or delayed
Bruising, cuts, or injuries from door closing on occupants

citations.title: Kia Carnival Sliding Door Sensor Lawsuit — CarComplaints

communityRecommendations.content: Even after the recall software update, supervise children closely around the sliding doors — the class action alleges the fix does not fully resolve the pinch sensor sensitivity issue.

Keep a written record of any incidents where the door fails to auto-reverse, including dates, photos of injuries, and dealer visit records — this documentation is critical if you need to file a warranty or legal claim.

before.title: Wind Noise / Air Leak from Front Door Window Seals Above ~45 MPH
before.description: Many Carnival owners, especially on lower trims (LX/LXS/LX Plus) that lack the thicker acoustic laminated front glass, report pronounced wind noise from the top rear corner of the front door windows starting around 45 mph and worsening with speed. Owners can often make the noise stop by pressing up on the window seal in that corner, indicating a weak seal or a door slightly out of adjustment from the factory.
before.solution: Dealers have addressed it under warranty by replacing the door weatherstrips and adding foam backing behind the strip that seals against the glass (reported ~90% improvement), and by re-adjusting the front door so it sits flush with the body. Upgrading to trims with acoustic laminated front glass, or aftermarket seal/foam kits, further reduces the noise.
symptoms: Wind whistle from front door window above 45 mph
Noise worsens at highway speed
Pressing on window seal stops the noise
Air leak near top rear corner of front glass

before.title: Spontaneous Windshield Cracking Without Impact
before.description: Numerous Kia Carnival owners report windshields cracking spontaneously without any visible impact from road debris. Cracks often appear near the base of the windshield or along the edges and spread rapidly across the entire glass. NHTSA received at least 14 complaints for the 2022 model year alone. Owners have reported difficulty obtaining replacement windshields due to stock shortages at dealerships, and Kia has generally denied warranty coverage claiming the cracks are from impact damage.
before.solution: Document the crack immediately with photos and note the location where it originates — spontaneous cracks typically start from the edge or base rather than a central impact point. File an NHTSA complaint to build the case record. Contact Kia customer service to request goodwill coverage. If denied, consider having an independent glass specialist assess whether the crack pattern is consistent with a manufacturing stress defect rather than impact.
symptoms: Windshield crack appearing with no visible impact point
Crack originating from edge or base of windshield
Crack spreading rapidly across windshield within hours or days
Cracking occurring during temperature changes or parked overnight
Multiple cracks appearing in the same general area

before.title: Wireless Qi Charging Pad Overheats Phones and Stops Charging
before.description: The center-console Qi wireless charging pad on 2022-2024 Carnivals routinely overheats phones (owners cite iPhone 15 Pro Max and others), triggering high-temperature warnings and thermal throttling so the phone gets hot to the touch and stops charging, especially on calls while charging. Owners note the pad lacks an active ventilation fan despite manual references to a cooling system, so heat has nowhere to go.
before.solution: Center the phone precisely on the pad (charging is weak near the rim), remove thick cases, and avoid charging while on speaker/video calls. Because there is no cooling fan, many owners switch to a wired cable in the adjacent USB port or use a ventilated/fan-cooled third-party wireless mount. No factory fix exists for the pad's lack of ventilation.
symptoms: Phone overheats on wireless pad
High-temperature warning while charging
Charging stops when phone gets hot
Slow or intermittent wireless charging
